**WARNING**: Machine-generated draft.

Empowerment measures how much an agent can do *to* the world.
A natural-looking dual, "plasticity", tries to measure how much the world can do *to the agent* — how much the agent's actions can be informed by what it senses.
The proposal on the table obtains plasticity by swapping the arguments of the mutual information in Klyubin-style empowerment.
This note shows that the swap is not innocent: the plasticity term is confounded by the agent's own plan, and can be large — in fact maximal — for an agent that senses nothing at all.
The fix is to treat the term causally, à la Ay–Polani, and the fixed version turns out to be estimable in this setting, because the interventions required are interventions on the agent's own actions.

## Setup

An agent interacts with an environment over a window $t, t+1, \dots, t+n$.
Write $W_k$ for the latent world state, $S_k$ for the sensor reading, and $A_k$ for the action at time $k$.
The world evolves as $W_{k+1} \sim P(\cdot \mid W_k, A_k)$ and the sensor reads $S_k \sim P(\cdot \mid W_k)$.
Actions are generated by a policy with private randomness $U$ (the "plan"): in **closed loop** $A_k$ may depend on $(S_{t:k}, U)$; in **open loop** $A_k$ depends on $U$ alone.
The joint distribution $p(a_{t:t+n})$ appearing in the definitions below is the marginal over action sequences that this policy induces.
Crucially, $U$ is independent of the environment noise and touches the world only through actions.

## Empowerment

$n$-step empowerment [@Klyubin2005All; @Klyubin2005Empowerment] is the capacity of the actuation channel — action sequence in, final sensor state out:

$$
\mathrm{Emp}_t \;=\; \max_{p(a_{t:t+n})} I\!\left(A_{t:t+n};\, S_{t+n}\right).
$$

One structural fact does all the work in what follows: under the maximizing $p$, the actions are **exogenous**.
Their only parent is $U$, so there is no back-door path from $A_{t:t+n}$ to $S_{t+n}$, and the observational mutual information coincides with the causal influence of actions on the future sensor state.
Empowerment never needed a $do$-operator because the channel input is something the agent sets by fiat.

## Plasticity

The proposed plasticity term inverts the arguments:

$$
\mathrm{Plas}_t \;=\; \max_{p(a_{t:t+n})} I\!\left(S_{t:t+n};\, A_{t+n}\right).
$$

The intended reading: how much can the eventual action be informed by the intervening sensor trajectory — an upper bound on the agent's willingness to adapt its policy to its environment.
For that reading to be the actual content of the formula, the dependence between $S_{t:t+n}$ and $A_{t+n}$ would have to flow through the sensor-to-action edges.
It need not.

## The confound

There are two routes by which $A_{t+n}$ can correlate with the sensor trajectory:

1. **Feedback**: $A_{t+n}$ reads the sensors ($S_j \to A_{t+n}$ edges). This is the intended route.
2. **The plan**: $A_{t+n}$ shares the source $U$ with earlier actions, and those earlier actions shaped the world that the sensors then read.

The second route survives in fully open loop.
In the open-loop graph (delete every dashed edge in @fig-pa-loop), take any $j > t$ and consider the path

$$
A_{t+n} \;\leftarrow\; U \;\rightarrow\; A_{j-1} \;\rightarrow\; W_j \;\rightarrow\; S_j .
$$

It contains one fork ($U$) and chains elsewhere, and nothing on it is conditioned, so it is open: $A_{t+n} \not\perp_d S_j$, and generically $I(S_{t:t+n}; A_{t+n}) > 0$.
An agent that senses nothing has positive "plasticity", because its plan is written into the world and the sensors read the plan back.
(Only the first reading $S_t$ is immune: every path into an action passes through $U$, which is disconnected from $W_t$.)

The confound is not merely a nuisance term; the maximization actively recruits it.

::: {#prp-saturation .proposition}
Suppose dynamics and sensors are deterministic and there is a set $\mathcal{A}' \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ of actions whose one-step traces are distinguishable, i.e. the map $a \mapsto s_{t+1}(a)$ is injective on $\mathcal{A}'$.
Then the open-loop policy that draws $V$ uniformly on $\mathcal{A}'$ and plays $A_t = A_{t+n} = V$ achieves
$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n};\, A_{t+n}\right) \;=\; \log \lvert \mathcal{A}' \rvert ,
$$
so if all actions leave distinguishable traces, $\mathrm{Plas}_t = \log \lvert \mathcal{A} \rvert$ — the maximum possible value of $H(A_{t+n})$ — with no sensor-to-action edge in the graph.
:::

::: {.proof}
$S_{t+1}$ is a deterministic injective function of $A_t = V$, so $H(A_{t+n} \mid S_{t:t+n}) \le H(V \mid S_{t+1}) = 0$, while $H(A_{t+n}) = \log\lvert\mathcal{A}'\rvert$.
The upper bound $I(S; A_{t+n}) \le H(A_{t+n}) \le \log\lvert\mathcal{A}\rvert$ is generic.
:::

So in any environment where actions leave legible marks — which is exactly the environments where empowerment is large — the plasticity term saturates trivially.
As a reward signal it would be Goodharted immediately: the optimal policy under the term is one that writes its plan into the environment and recovers it from the sensors, which requires no sensitivity to the environment at all.

**The obvious fix fails.**
One might condition away the earlier actions: use $I(S_{t:t+n}; A_{t+n} \mid A_{t:t+n-1})$.
In open loop this works — conditioning on $A_{t:t+n-1}$ blocks every fork path above, since each passes through some earlier action as a non-collider.
But the definition is supposed to cover closed-loop policies, and once feedback edges exist, each $A_j$ is a *collider* on

$$
S_j \;\rightarrow\; A_j \;\leftarrow\; U \;\rightarrow\; A_{t+n},
$$

and conditioning on $A_j$ opens that path.
Concretely: if earlier actions read the sensors but the final action ignores them, then given the earlier actions' values, the sensor readings carry information about $U$, and hence about $A_{t+n}$.
The conditional mutual information is positive although the final action does no sensing.
Neither the marginal nor the conditional observational quantity isolates the feedback edges.

## Repair 1: directed information

For two processes $X_{1:n}$ and $Y_{1:n}$ observed on a common clock, Massey's *directed information* [@Massey1990Causality] is

$$
I\!\left(X_{1:n} \to Y_{1:n}\right) \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^{n} I\!\left(X_{1:k};\, Y_k \,\middle|\, Y_{1:k-1}\right).
$$

Compare the chain rule for ordinary mutual information, $I(X_{1:n}; Y_{1:n}) = \sum_k I(X_{1:n}; Y_k \mid Y_{1:k-1})$: the only change is that the $k$-th term sees $X_{1:k}$ rather than all of $X_{1:n}$.
Each $Y_k$ is credited only with dependence on the $X$'s that *precede* it, so the quantity is asymmetric — $I(X \to Y) \neq I(Y \to X)$ in general — and it decomposes the symmetric mutual information into the flow in each direction [@Massey2005Conservation].
It is the natural measure of how much one process feeds forward into another when both are unrolling in time.

Applied to the sensor process feeding the action process on our window,

$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} I\!\left(S_{t:t+k};\, A_{t+k} \,\middle|\, A_{t:t+k-1}\right),
$$

this is the standard aggregate measure of feedback.
Under any open-loop policy every term vanishes: given the earlier actions, the sensor trajectory depends only on environment noise, which is independent of $U$, so $S_{t:t+k} \perp A_{t+k} \mid A_{t:t+k-1}$.
Conversely, if any action reads any sensor, the corresponding term is positive.
So directed information is zero if and only if the policy is effectively open loop — it is a sound *detector* of sensing, which the raw plasticity term is not.

Its limitation is attribution.
The final term of the sum is exactly the conditional mutual information whose collider problem was just described, so directed information can assign positive flow "into $A_{t+n}$" when only earlier actions sensed anything.
The total is meaningful; the per-step decomposition is not.

## Repair 2: causal information flow (Ay–Polani)

Ay and Polani's information flow [@Ay2008Information] replaces conditioning with intervention.
To measure what the final action actually absorbs from the sensors, sever the back-door by force: fix the earlier actions by $do(a_{t:t+n-1})$ and evaluate

$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n};\, A_{t+n}\right) \quad \text{in} \quad p\!\left(\cdot \,\middle|\, do(a_{t:t+n-1})\right),
$$

averaged (or maximized) over the intervention values.
Under the intervention, earlier actions are no longer children of $U$ or of the sensors, so the collider path is gone along with the fork paths: the quantity is zero precisely when $A_{t+n}$ ignores the sensors, and positive precisely when it reads them.
This is the per-step attribution that directed information cannot give.
The two repairs are complementary: directed information for the total feedback flow of a policy, interventional flow for crediting it to particular actions.

## What can actually be estimated

Interventional quantities are in general not identifiable from observational data, so it is fair to ask whether the $do$ above is an estimand or a wish.
Here it is an estimand, for a structural reason: the interventions are on the agent's own actions, and in the perception–action loop the actions have no unobserved confounders *by construction*.
Every parent of $A_k$ is either the observed history $S_{t:k}, A_{t:k-1}$ or the private noise $U$, and $U$ is independent of the environment.
That is sequential ignorability, so the g-formula applies and the interventional distribution factorizes into observational kernels:

$$
p\!\left(s_{t:t+n} \,\middle|\, do(a_{t:t+n-1})\right) \;=\; \prod_{k} p\!\left(s_k \,\middle|\, s_{t:k-1},\, a_{t:k-1}\right),
$$

each factor an observable conditional of logged trajectories.
The binding constraints are the standard ones:

1. **Positivity.** The logging policy must give every relevant action sequence positive probability given every history. A deterministic logger kills identification off its support, and the effective sample size of importance-weighted estimates decays geometrically in the window length $n$. Long-horizon plasticity is identifiable in principle and miserable in practice.
2. **No unlogged sensors.** Ignorability holds because we know what the policy read. If the agent has an input channel that was not logged and that correlates with the world, the g-formula is silently wrong.

Three distinct objects, in increasing order of what they cost to obtain:

- **Directed information of a deployed policy.** A functional of the on-policy joint distribution. Estimable directly from that policy's own rollouts; no adjustment, no off-policy correction. Interpretation: how many bits of environmental contingency this agent in fact absorbs into its actions per window — realized responsiveness.
- **Interventional flow into a given action.** Needs the $do$-distribution: either run the interventions (an agent can always randomize its own actions), or identify from logs via the g-formula subject to the two caveats. Interpretation: how much this particular action is steered by the world, with the agent's self-signalling surgically removed.
- **Plasticity as a capacity.** Both definitions above sit inside a $\max_{p}$, and a capacity was never going to be passively estimated from someone else's logs: computing it *means* optimizing over policies you get to run, exactly as empowerment is computed by Blahut–Arimoto or by policy optimization, as in discounted-empowerment pre-training [@Schneider2025InformationTheoretic]. Once you are running policies, you can sample any interventional distribution directly. The $do$-operator costs nothing that the $\max$ had not already charged. Interpretation: the feedback capacity of the loop — how many bits the environment *could* impress on the agent's actions, a property of sensor channel plus dynamics, dual to empowerment as the actuation capacity.

## Interpretation, and families of agents

The asymmetry underneath all of this: empowerment's channel input is exogenous, plasticity's is not.
Actions are interventions; sensor readings are consequences.
Inverting the arguments of a mutual information does not invert the causal semantics, which is why empowerment gets away without causal machinery and plasticity does not.

With the repaired term, the original motivation goes through.
An objective family

$$
J_\beta \;=\; \mathrm{Emp}_t \;+\; \beta \cdot I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right)
$$

trades control over the world against steerability by the world: $\beta = 0$ is the pure empowerment agent, and the plasticity slot pays for actions contingent on observation.
With the *unrepaired* term in the second slot the family collapses — by @prp-saturation the optimizer saturates the plasticity slot through self-signalling, and every $\beta$ yields approximately the pure empowerment agent.
"Contingent on observation" is still a slogan, though.
The next section computes what the slot actually pays for.

## What the plasticity slot actually rewards

Apply the chain rule $H(A_{t:t+n}) = \sum_k H(A_{t+k} \mid A_{t:t+k-1})$ to the directed information:

$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right)
\;=\; H\!\left(A_{t:t+n}\right) \;-\; \underbrace{\sum_{k=0}^{n} H\!\left(A_{t+k} \,\middle|\, A_{t:t+k-1},\, S_{t:t+k}\right)}_{\text{causally conditioned entropy } H(A \,\|\, S)} .
$$

So maximizing the term means doing exactly two things: raise the total behavioural entropy $H(A_{t:t+n})$, and eliminate the part of it not resolvable from the percepts available at the moment of acting.
The second part, $H(A \,\|\, S)$, is the residual plan noise — randomness that $U$ injects into actions beyond what the sensors dictate — and the objective counts it *against* the agent.
At the optimum of the second lever the identity becomes exact:

::: {#prp-transcription .proposition}
If the policy is a deterministic function of sensor history, $A_{t+k} = \pi_k(S_{t:t+k})$, then
$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right) \;=\; H\!\left(A_{t:t+n}\right),
$$
and this entropy is entirely environment-sourced: writing $\varepsilon$ for the exogenous noise variables of the loop (initial state $W_t$, transition noise, sensor noise), every action is a measurable function of $\varepsilon$, so $H(A_{t:t+n}) = I(A_{t:t+n}; \varepsilon)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Determinism makes every summand of $H(A \,\|\, S)$ zero, giving the first claim.
For the second, induct along the window: $S_{t:t+k}$ is a measurable function of $(\varepsilon, A_{t:t+k-1})$, and each $A_{t+j}$ with $j < k$ is by hypothesis a function of $S_{t:t+j}$, so all of $A_{t:t+k}$ is a function of $\varepsilon$ alone; then $H(A) = I(A; \varepsilon)$ because entropy of a function of $\varepsilon$ is mutual information with $\varepsilon$.
:::

That is the precise content of the reward: **bits of exogenous randomness transcribed into behaviour per window**.
The causal conditioning on $A_{t:t+k-1}$ is what enforces "exogenous" — sensor variation that the agent's own past actions produced is conditioned away, which is the same echo-suppression that motivated the repair.
Three consequences fix its character.

**It rewards reacting, not adapting.**
Any injective transcription of disturbances scores; nothing requires the response to be useful.
A device that deterministically mirrors its noisy input — a thermometer driving a dial — is optimal.
This is not a defect relative to empowerment; it is the same defect.
Both are task-free channel objectives, and just as empowerment counts influence without asking whether the influenced states matter, plasticity counts responsiveness without asking whether the responses do.
The "willingness to adapt" gloss imports an intentional reading the functional does not contain; what it contains is sensitivity.

**It penalizes exploration noise.**
The $-H(A \,\|\, S)$ term actively punishes stochasticity that is not sensor-driven.
Large $\beta$ therefore pushes toward *deterministic* reactive policies — close to the opposite of the open, exploratory agent the word plasticity suggests.
An agent that dithers is, by this measure, less plastic than a thermostat, because its dithering is plan noise and plan noise is subtracted.

**Its budget is the environment's noise supply.**
By @prp-transcription the reward is capped by $H(\varepsilon)$ as seen through the sensors.
In the extreme case this cap is zero:

::: {#prp-zerocap .proposition}
If dynamics and sensors are deterministic and the initial state $W_t$ is known, then $I(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}) = 0$ for *every* policy.
:::

::: {.proof}
Given $A_{t:t+k-1}$, the trajectory $S_{t:t+k}$ is a deterministic function of $(W_t, A_{t:t+k-1})$ and hence constant; conditioning on a constant changes no entropy, so every summand $I(S_{t:t+k}; A_{t+k} \mid A_{t:t+k-1})$ vanishes.
:::

Set @prp-zerocap beside @prp-saturation and the raw and repaired terms disagree maximally on the same test case: in a deterministic, fully legible world, raw plasticity is $\log\lvert\mathcal{A}\rvert$ — its largest possible value — while repaired plasticity is identically zero.
The raw term reads a noiseless world as maximal adaptability because self-signalling works best there; the repaired term reads it correctly as offering nothing to adapt *to*.
Deterministic worlds are also where empowerment is largest and cheapest to compute, so the two slots of $J_\beta$ pull toward different environments as well as different policies: $\mathrm{Emp}_t$ counts the state distinctions the agent's actions can create, the plasticity slot counts the action distinctions the world's disturbances can create, and $\beta$ prices bits of control against bits of transcription.

The same discounting that @Schneider2025InformationTheoretic apply to empowerment horizons applies verbatim here: a $\lambda$-discounted sum of window-$k$ directed informations gives a discounted plasticity that weights short-horizon against long-horizon responsiveness, and the $\lambda \to 0$ and Abel $\lambda \to 1$ limits play the same roles as for discounted empowerment.
